hero.headline: FRANCE MARCH ON, MBAPPÉ CATCHES MESSI
hero.standfirst: A missed penalty, then perfection: Kylian Mbappé curled France ahead on the hour, set up Dembélé six minutes later, and the 2022 semi-final rematch went exactly the way of the first meeting. France are in the last four without conceding momentum once — and the Golden Boot race is level at the top again.

facts.text: France's xG of 3.04 to Morocco's 0.14 — as one-sided as a quarter-final gets
Mbappé missed a first-half penalty — then answered with a goal and an assist inside six second-half minutes
Six wins from six without extra time — no other team in the bracket can say it

yesterday.report: For an hour Morocco's famous wall held, and Mbappé's first-half penalty miss — shades of Messi and Egypt — let Boston believe in another African miracle. Then the hour struck. Mbappé collected the ball on the left, cut in, and curled a shot into the far corner that no goalkeeper reaches: his 8th of the tournament and the 20th of his World Cup career, one behind Messi's all-time count.
yesterday.report2: Six minutes later he turned provider, slipping in Dembélé for the fifth goal of the winger's tournament, and the tie was done. The final numbers — 21 shots to 4, eight on target to one, an xG of 3.04 against 0.14 — read like a training exercise. France are the first team into the last four, still perfect, still yet to need a single minute of extra time.

star.name: Kylian Mbappé
star.line: The penalty miss would have haunted a lesser tournament. Instead: a world-class winner, an assist, level with Messi on 8 — and a semi-final on Tuesday to settle the argument.

aside.name: Ousmane Dembélé
aside.line: Five tournament goals from the wing, and the quiet half of the deadliest duo in the bracket.

yesterday.whatItMeans: France meet tonight's Spain–Belgium winner in Tuesday's Dallas semi-final. Morocco's second straight deep run ends at France's hands, again.

today.kicker: QF2 · THE WALL AGAINST THE WAVE
today.preview: The cleanest matchup of the round: Spain have not conceded in five games — goalkeeper Unai Simón's 609 unbreached minutes are a World Cup record — while Belgium arrive on an 18-match unbeaten run having just handed the USA the most emphatic knockout defeat by anyone left in the bracket. Something must give, and whatever gives, France are waiting for the survivor in Dallas.

keyMan.name: Unai Simón
keyMan.line: 609 minutes, five clean sheets, a record already his. Belgium's four-goal night in Seattle is precisely the storm his record has never faced.

factors.label: FORM
factors.text: Spain: five clean sheets in five games and control of every match they've played. Belgium: an 18-game unbeaten run and a 4–1 statement against the hosts.

factors.label: HEAD-TO-HEAD
factors.text: Two World Cup meetings, honours even: Belgium won the 1986 quarter-final on penalties after 1–1; Spain took the 1990 group game 2–1.

factors.label: FITNESS & FATIGUE
factors.text: Spain report a full squad. Belgium's Amadou Onana limped off against the USA with a knee problem and remains a doubt in their engine room.

factors.label: WHERE THE MONEY IS
factors.text: Kalshi's live market ($1.4m traded): Spain 60%, the draw 25%, Belgium 17% in regulation — almost exactly the France–Morocco shape from last night, and that one obeyed the money.

prediction.verdict: The record says Spain don't concede; Seattle says Belgium have finally woken up. We think Simón's wall bends but doesn't break when it matters — Spain, with the first goal past them of the tournament as the consolation Belgium take home. If Onana misses out, add a goal to Spain's side.
